postconditions.statement: crew context + handoff + generator + guard + door refusal + M1 probe loaded; handoff complete; keys-vs-prose question settled with a reason drawn from what compile_spec carries
postconditions.satisfied_by: Loaded: handoff (complete -- task, scope, exclusions, evidence, test mode, stop conditions, return format all present), both specs, scripts/generate_spine.py, tests/test_cli_retirement_guard.py, mcp_spine_server.py _rebind_refusal/_spine_bind, notes-1.md M1. SCHEMA QUESTION SETTLED: prose only, no new keys. Reason from the consumer, not from taste -- generate_spine._compile_gate builds each compiled task from a FIXED field list (id, title, imperative, preconditions, postconditions, constraints, directives, child_checklist, status, status_detail, result, finding, evidence, rework_count) and compile_spec builds the top level from a fixed list too, so any new spec key is silently DROPPED at compile; spec_shape_faults has no unknown-key fault, so it would not even refuse loudly. TOML comments are dropped the same way. The only authored text that reaches an agent is title, imperative, constraints, condition statement, and qualitative `because` (compile_condition folds it into the statement). Door vocabulary must therefore live in imperative + constraints to be read at all.

triage_candidates.statement: The g3 gate's own closing check in the handoff cannot pass, for a reason unrelated to this gate's work. Its last clause is `! grep -oE '(skills|specs|[.]agent-work)/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+' /tmp/g3-guard.log | grep -qv '^skills/workbench/'`, but the guard's own failure message embeds a census line -- "(101 under skills/, 2 under specs/, 113 under .agent-work/templates/)" -- and `.agent-work/templates/` matches that address pattern while not starting with `skills/workbench/`. Measured on the UNMODIFIED tree before I touched anything: the filtered grep prints `.agent-work/templates/` twice (once per failing test) and exits 0, so the negated check is false at baseline. It only passes once the guard is entirely green, i.e. after lane D2's fenced files are swept -- which the handoff says is g5-final's job, not this gate's. Commander decision: narrow the address pattern (e.g. require a filename character after the final slash, or grep only `specs/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+`, which is what the handoff's own Verification Commands section uses and which is clean), or accept the gate on the specs-only form.

specs/reviewer.spine.toml (type = survey) carries config_ref = "docs/agents/engine-config.json" while skills/explorer/templates/CYCLE.template.json -- also a survey -- deliberately DROPS the key, with tests/test_explorer_templates.py:242-247 pinning the reason ("a survey never consults rework_cap ... the key is dropped rather than pointed at a file a fresh install won't have"). Two shipped survey artifacts state opposite conventions. Separately, docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md:35-38 rules the missing file deliberately fine, so "create the config" is likely the wrong fix. Staged in full at .agent-work/567-d1/triage-candidates/engine-config-json-absent.md (g3 addendum). Not fixed here: half is free, half is a rework-cap defaults decision for a human.

why_trail.why: The keys-vs-prose question is decided by what the compiler carries, not by preference: _compile_gate and compile_spec both construct their output dicts from fixed field lists, so a new spec key reaches no reader and spec_shape_faults would not refuse it -- a silent drop, the worst of both. Prose in imperative and constraints is the only text that reaches a dispatched role. Second finding from the same read: an UNBOUND door binds its own plan fine (I just did it, and the identity came from the spine's own work_id rather than from anything I supplied), so the honest doctrine is conditioned on holding a lease, not on the checklist being 'second'.

The vocabulary states both halves as one rule rather than as a capability plus an apology: the door reaches the spine you hold a lease on, and you hold exactly one, so a second checklist is out of reach BY the same rule that makes the door work at all. It also carries the case the handoff's premise missed and I measured first-hand this run -- an unbound door binds one spine and drives it identically, with the identity derived from the spine's own work id -- so the doctrine is conditioned on holding a lease, not on a checklist being 'second'. Where it landed is settled by the consumer: imperative and constraints are two of the five fields _compile_gate carries, and a header comment records why a new key was not the answer.

The reviewer text is the same rule in the survey dialect, not a copy: a survey item closes through spine_survey_result and the engine literally refuses the gated verb ("advance is for gated checklists; use record", checklist_engine.py:2621), so naming spine_advance here would have handed a reviewer a verb it cannot use. It also points the "what if these items are wrong" case at r6-fowler's existing REPAIR PATH rather than inventing a second convention.

The prose choice is now proven rather than argued. Both specs pass all five generator layers (tomllib, spec-shape, compile, probes, the validate_spine oracle) and write a spine; the new door vocabulary is present in the COMPILED tasks' own imperative and constraints, and the header comment that explains the decision is measured absent from both compiled files (0 occurrences) -- which is exactly the reason a new key would have been the wrong answer: it would have been dropped just as silently, with no fault to say so.

The result carries what the handoff asked for (before/after for both files, the schema decision reasoned from _compile_gate's carried-field list, the guard run with no specs/ address, the config_ref finding with the CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md ruling and the CYCLE.template.json precedent) plus two things the Commander needs before closing g3: the gate's own closing check is red at baseline because its address grep matches the guard's own census string, and the handoff's premise that dispatched crews cannot reach the door for their own plan is false -- this plan was driven end to end through the door from a spine:null dispatch, with the identity derived from the plan's work_id. The config_ref was deliberately not fixed: half of it is a defaults decision for a human and the schema doc blesses the current state in writing.
